title: One Ångström Inside Dorothy Hodgkin's Cobalt Cage — Whipple, Minot & Murphy's 1926 Liver Cure, Castle's Intrinsic Factor–Cubilin Lock (PDB 3KQ4, 2PMV), Dorothy Hodgkin's 181-Atom Corrin Ring, Methylmalonyl-CoA Mutase Co–C Homolysis (PDB 1REQ, 4REQ, 3BIC), MMA vs. Homocysteine, N2O Myelopathy & Canine CUBN / Feline EPI

teenKit.tldr: Vitamin B12 is an invisible daily speck of chemistry required to prevent a total systemic and neurological collapse. Its complex atomic cage—mapped by Nobel laureate Dorothy Hodgkin—holds a rare carbon-cobalt bond that runs our entire metabolism.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Without this single microscopic molecule and its elaborate cellular delivery system, human bodies and animal companions alike face irreversible nerve damage and fatal disease.
keyTakeaways: In 1926, pernicious anemia was 100% fatal until a radical cure involving massive daily doses of raw liver was discovered.
Dorothy Hodgkin used X-ray crystallography to map the 181-atom corrin ring, revealing the cobalt atom at the beating heart of vitamin B12.
Nitrous oxide ("laughing gas") can destroy B12 functionality, leading to a catastrophic spinal cord breakdown known as N2O myelopathy.

vocab.meaning: A historically 100% fatal disease caused by the body's inability to absorb vitamin B12, leading to severe systemic and neurological failure.
An intricate 181-atom molecular cage engineered around a single cobalt atom to stabilize vitamin B12.
A specialized protein produced in the stomach that binds to vitamin B12 so the small intestine can safely absorb it.
The splitting of a chemical bond where each shared electron goes back to its original atom, a key mechanism of B12 enzymes.

quiz.question: What unusual food cure did George Minot and William Murphy successfully use to treat pernicious anemia in 1926?
quiz.explanation: Minot and Murphy discovered that eating massive quantities of raw liver inexplicably cured a previously 100% fatal disease.

quiz.question: Which metal atom sits right at the center of Dorothy Hodgkin's 181-atom corrin ring for vitamin B12?
quiz.explanation: Cobalt is the crucial transition metal caged inside the corrin ring, enabling B12's unique catalytic properties.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of the stomach's 'Intrinsic Factor' in relation to vitamin B12?
options: It destroys excess bacteria in the gut
It converts B12 into active homocysteine
It locks onto B12 so the intestine can absorb it
It synthesizes the corrin ring from scratch
quiz.explanation: Intrinsic factor binds to vitamin B12, forming a complex that locks onto intestinal receptors (cubilin) for proper absorption.
